claims.text: Nano-sized precipitates introduced by controlled thermo-mechanical processing could improve the dynamic mechanical performance of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Controlled thermo-mechanical processing can produce the proposed nano-sized precipitates in FeNiCrMn.
Mn2O3 is a suitable nano-sized precipitate for modifying FeNiCrMn.
The nano-sized precipitates would impede dislocation motion.
The proposed precipitates would strengthen grain boundaries.
Precipitate-mediated restriction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary strengthening would improve yield strength under loading.
The precipitate modification would improve ductility as well as yield strength, rather than producing a strength-ductility trade-off.
The modified alloy could exhibit a strength increase of up to 20% relative to unmodified Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The modified alloy could exhibit a ductility increase of up to 30% relative to unmodified Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The proposed improvement would apply from -20°C to 800°C.
The proposed improvement would apply at strain rates from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^-1 s^-1.
Mechanical behavior in related Cantor-alloy systems varies with temperature.
The cited prior studies support precipitation strengthening by Mn2O3 in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The exact precipitate amount and distribution needed for optimal performance are unknown.

contradictions.description: The study is repeatedly described as dynamic loading, but the specified strain-rate range of 10^-3 to 10^-1 s^-1 is ordinarily quasi-static to moderately rate-dependent rather than a conventional dynamic or high-strain-rate regime.
The hypothesis promises introduction of a 'specific amount' of precipitates, but no amount is supplied and the uncertainty field states that the required amount is unknown.
